items.summary: Benchmark paper that tests frontier AI agents across stages of professional design work, from brief to delivery.
items.whyItMatters: Shows where agents still fall short of a full design workflow.

items.summary: Paper on recovering written skill documents from model adapters, relevant to how agent skills are packaged and inspected.
items.whyItMatters: Niche, but touches how skill files relate to model behavior.

items.summary: Descriptive analysis of how viral, educational and commercial uses of LLM image tools differ, built to protect user privacy.
items.whyItMatters: Gives a picture of how people actually use image generation.

items.summary: Paper tracing how backdoors can enter agent skills during automated skill optimization.
items.whyItMatters: A caution if you let tools rewrite your skill files.

items.summary: NVIDIA post on faster image generation with a FLUX model on Blackwell GPUs.
items.whyItMatters: Faster image models mean shorter iteration loops for visual work.

items.summary: Vercel announces that Chat SDK agents can stream generative UI using its json-render format.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete path for agents to return real interface components.

items.summary: Figma conversation between its CEO and a guest on the human role when creating with AI.
items.whyItMatters: Context on how Figma frames the designer role as tools change.

items.summary: NN/g defines the term agent harness, giving UX teams shared vocabulary for agent-based products.
items.whyItMatters: Shared terms help you scope and critique agent product UX.

items.summary: Figma workflow walkthrough on testing ideas using code layers together with its agent.
items.whyItMatters: Shows a hands-on way to prototype with Figma's agent.

items.summary: Paper proposing context-aware autoregressive image generation and reporting emerging reasoning behavior.
items.whyItMatters: Background research; little direct effect on design work yet.

items.summary: Figma engineering post about running sandboxes at scale.
items.whyItMatters: Hints at the infrastructure behind agent features in Figma.

items.summary: Lovable explains how it has rebuilt its AI app builder repeatedly as models change.
items.whyItMatters: Useful view of how fast UI-generation products shift under you.

items.summary: Hugging Face post on training a small model to produce slide decks that follow a given design language.
items.whyItMatters: Points to design-system-aware generation on small models.

items.summary: Essay asking who designs the stop controls for AI agents.
items.whyItMatters: A prompt to design interruption and override for agent UIs.

items.summary: Report on an indie game that markets itself as hand-drawn and anti-AI and found a large audience.
items.whyItMatters: Signals audience appetite for visibly human-made art.

items.summary: Manifesto-style essay on design work after the AI hype cycle.
items.whyItMatters: Opinion; a view on where design goes next.

items.summary: Fast Company covers renewed debate about a Dior holiday ad and AI use.
items.whyItMatters: Another data point on audience reaction to AI in ads.

items.summary: Jakob Nielsen's roundup of short UX notes, including a section on slow AI.
items.whyItMatters: Quick scan of current UX thinking; not new research.

items.summary: Essay on a specific interaction question raised by an AI-drawn side panel and filters.
items.whyItMatters: Shows the small behavior gaps AI-generated UI leaves open.

items.summary: Essay arguing exploratory search still beats a single AI answer.
items.whyItMatters: Supports designing for exploration in AI search.

items.summary: Smashing Magazine guide to making immersive LLM chat interfaces more accessible.
items.whyItMatters: Practical accessibility guidance for chat-style AI products.
